meta.title: P2N2222A NPN General-Purpose Amplifier/Switch Transistor
meta.summary: 40 V, 600 mA NPN small-signal transistor in TO-92 (C-B-E pinout), the classic 2N2222A die. Usable as a linear amplifier (f_T ≥ 300 MHz, h_FE 100–300 at 150 mA) or as a saturated switch up to a few hundred mA. In free air the 625 mW / 200 °C/W TO-92 rating, not the 600 mA current rating, is usually the real limit; h_FE collapses above ≈200 mA, so drive switches at I_C/I_B ≈ 10.

calculators.title: Thermal limits & derating
calculators.description: Derated maximum dissipation for the chosen thermal path; uses R_θ so that P_D(max) reaches zero at T_J = 150 °C (equivalent to the datasheet's 5 mW/°C and 12 mW/°C derating).

notes: P2N2222A pinout is 1 = collector, 2 = base, 3 = emitter (TO-92 Style 17). This differs from the EBC pinout of many other 2N2222A TO-92 parts.
h_FE, V_CE(sat), V_BE(sat) limits at 150 mA and 500 mA are pulse-tested (PW ≤ 300 µs, duty ≤ 2 %); continuous operation at those currents self-heats the die.
All characteristic curves are typical values at T_J = 25 °C unless a temperature is given; use the guaranteed minimum h_FE (not the typical curve) to size base drive.
Figure 3 h_FE curves are labelled with T_J; calculators use the estimated self-heated T_J (T_A + V_CE·I_C·R_θ), clamped to −55…125 °C.
The maximum ratings derate linearly: 625 mW − 5 mW/°C above T_A = 25 °C (free air, R_θJA = 200 °C/W), or 1.5 W − 12 mW/°C above T_C = 25 °C (R_θJC = 83.3 °C/W).

Switching-time curves (Figures 5 and 6) use V_CC = 30 V, I_C/I_B = 10 and, for turn-off, equal forward and reverse base currents (I_B1 = I_B2). Typical microcontroller drive without a speed-up capacitor turns off considerably slower.
Figure 7 (NF vs frequency) shows four almost coincident curves; only their upper envelope is digitized.
In the PDF the electrical table prints µ as 'm' in the text layer (ICBO µA, hoe µmhos, NF at 100 µA, pulse width 300 µs); the rendered page shows µ, which is what is used here.
Fits marked 'Derived' are closed-form approximations of the digitized curves, not datasheet equations.
